title.analysis: Authentic title "The SpaceX IPO Is About To Flip Your 401k - Most People Are Not Ready" is an urgent news-hook frame. The script's actual argument is that SpaceX is not in most 401(k)s (S&P 500 rules exclude it until at least 2027) and that the real change is the August 2025 private-assets executive order; the title's "flip your 401k" is delivered only indirectly.

script.opening_words: The two smartest things you can do about the SpaceX IPO are buy it or completely ignore it. One of those is a trap, and most people are about to pick the wrong one. On June 12th, 2026, a guy named Logan opened his Robinhood app and bought four shares of the most hyped IPO in human history, SpaceX, ticker SPACE, $135 a share. It closed the day up 19% and he went to bed convinced he'd finally gotten in
script.ending_words: that retirement account. Read the fine print before the fine print starts reading you. The rocket's going to be fine. The question is whether you are. And as always, just a quick reminder, I'm not a financial advisor and none of this is financial advice. It's just me doing way too much math for educational purposes only. What you do with your own money is on you. Make it count.
script.analysis: Full 47641 canonical characters read. A single-narrator 52-minute explainer with two composites (Logan buys IPO shares; Dana owns a target-date fund): the IPO facts, retail allocation, S&P 500 eligibility rules and the 4 June 2026 rejection, the Nasdaq-100 and MSCI exceptions, index-inclusion forced buying (Tesla), lockup risk, the August 2025 executive order, a steelman, three problems (fees, illiquidity, late-stage access), valuation (94x revenue; Morningstar $780B), shrinking public markets, the players and skeptics, side-door funds (DXYZ, ARK, Baron), IPO first-day history, the Logan/Dana payoff, four actions and a community promotion. Core facts verify; the 70,000% and 62,000% figures, the SPACE ticker and the Tesla run-up are wrong.
